blocks.text: A2-22 · Notices, forms, ads, emails
Lesson overview

An important part of the written language that you will encounter is "practical": notices on an office door, forms to fill out, ads, work emails and messages between friends. They are short texts, almost always without vowels, with fixed formulas that repeat themselves: ⁧الرَّجَاءُ عَدَمُ⁩ …, ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ …, ⁧مُغْلَقٌ لِلصِّيَانَةِ⁩ , ⁧السَّيِّدُ⁩ … ⁧المُحْتَرَمُ⁩ , ⁧تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ خَالِصِ التَّحِيَّاتِ⁩ . In this unit you learn to recognize and use these formulas, to distinguish the formal register from the informal one, and to write a full formal email. A week.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. read notices and signs with their formulas ( ⁧الرَّجَاءُ⁩ , ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ , ⁧يُمْنَعُ⁩ , ⁧عَدَمُ⁩ , ⁧حَتَّى إِشْعَارٍ آخَرَ⁩ );
2. fill in an administrative form with the most frequent fields;
3. write a formal email (object, greeting, request, attachments, closure) and an informal one;
4. understand short voice ads and messages;
5. read practical texts of 200–300 words without vowels.

6. Pronunciation

Read a warning. Warnings are read in pause, word by word, with the internal vowels: ar-raǧāʾ ʿadam at- tadḫīn. The maṣdar after ⁧الرَّجَاء⁩ and ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ is the key point: locate it before reading. Long formulas. wa-tafaḍḍalū bi-qabūli fāʾiqi l-iḥtirām: divide it into three groups (wa-tafaḍḍalū / bi-qabūli / fāʾiqi l-iḥtirām) and repeat it until it flows.
